chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: Jelly Roll's partner Anita and the quarrel with Bricktop
summary: Anita, Dink Johnson's sister, was Jelly Roll's long-time partner; the singer he quarreled with at the Cadillac was Bricktop, and Spikes calls his stories windy.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: When you first met him in Oklahoma, I read in one of these accounts, that he was travelling with a....a comedy partner, a woman. Who was that?
Uh, well, no, when I first met him, he was just piano player, and then when my brother and I went with the show, we sent for Jelly, and then he brought the woman with him.

SPIKES - 155
Reel 5
Page 7
And she was a comedian?
They done a little act--woman and wife and husband, you know?
Oh, so she was his wife? Then?
She was with him.
I see. What was her name?
I don't know.
It wasn't the same woman he was with later...here?
No, no, no. This was a... This woman that you talking about there, that he was with so long was Dink Johnson's sister.
Oh. Oh, I see. I didn't know that. That's Anita?
Anita. Yeah.
And he talks about having an argument with somebody named Bright Red. Apparently she was a singer at the Cadillac ...an entertainer.
That's Red...uh, Brick...uh, Red...er, Brick... Bricktop!
Bricktop?
Yeah, Bricktop. That's who he's talkin' about.

Ohhhh....Ohhhhh...Oohhhhh, I see, 'cause he mentions Bricktop later on but he doesn't say that this was Bricktop he had the argument with. He says she was "stuffin' tip money in her stocking and not sharing it" with him, and so he tried to turn her in, and instead, he got fired, and, at that point, he went out to Watts

SPIKES - 156

and took all the business away from the Cadillac Cafe, and it closed.
Is that right?

Well, Jelly Roll, you know, he was a bag of wind.
He's liable to say anything...but he's talkin' about Bricktop--the famous
Bricktop.
